primary_source.source_hypothesis_boundary: BEG works with algebraically closed characteristic-zero constants and smooth connected affine varieties. The application uses affine m-space, an injective m-variable polynomial position algebra, and an explicit constant-field descent argument. No positive spectral rank is needed for finite field degree.
primary_source.proof_dependency_note: BEG Section 2.2 uses finite-dimensionality of holonomic D-module endomorphisms, citing Borel et al., Algebraic D-modules (1988). This record imports the exact BEG theorem; it does not claim an independent foundational proof of that D-module fact.

written_arguments: Centralizer finite field theorem in the actual scalar finite-PBW algebra, without centralizer finite generation or individual conjugates.
Explicit spectral-module action and End identification, with the opposite ring made explicit.
Faithful scalar extension descent from algebraically closed constants.
Every positive spectral rank is divisible by the centralizer field degree.
In the QTB1 deformation setting with actual individual conjugates, a positive spectral rank at most two forces polynomial centralizer and full finite completion.
The low-rank corollary has a direct UFD quadratic obstruction proof and does not require purity or the characteristic-zero affine-space covering theorem.

A finite collection of positive spectral ranks in exact finite Weyl polarizations has gcd divisible by the centralizer field degree; gcd one or two forces polynomial centralizer and full finite completion under the stated QTB1 mate hypotheses.

algebraic_controls.conclusion: Spectral rank zero in the positional polarization despite centralizer field degree one; source localization inverts x-u.
Fourier-equivalent position has spectral rank one, so rank is polarization dependent.
